changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For finance buyers (CFO, controller) at distributors and B2B sellers, open the first call with reconciliation in their words: 'Know where every deposit came from, matched to the invoice in your ERP, without a week of month-end archaeology.' Say 'deposits', not 'payouts' or 'payments'. When the inbound is about checkout, ask about month-end close and deposit matching on the first call.
changes.why: Reconciliation was the only message that landed, and the CFO described her problem as 'I just want to know where my money is' and 'the deposits', never as 'payments', so the same capability should be framed around deposits and month-end effort.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers, replace the cited study with an offer: 'Send us one month of your statements and we'll cost your month-end: the matching hours and the unmatched deposits you write off.' Make the reconciliation-cost model a standard SE working session, and save the resulting figures so they can be reused.
changes.why: The deal went from 'Dead' to 'paperwork' only after the SE costed the customer's own statements, and the CFO accepted it as 'my number, not yours', which an independent vendor study cannot be.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: Stop opening first calls with M1 for finance buyers at distributors and B2B sellers. Lead with M9 as reworded above, and keep 'infrastructure' as internal language.
changes.why: The standard opener of 'Financial infrastructure, global growth, all the currencies' was met with silence, and nobody on the customer side said 'infrastructure'.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For wholesale and distributor buyers, do not send retail or software case studies. Until we have a wholesale distributor story ('wholesale, invoices, that kind of business'), offer the own-data costing session or a peer reference call instead. Prioritize capturing a distributor customer story and reference.
changes.why: The CFO asked twice to speak with another distributor, and the retail case study backfired ('this is a company that sells sweaters'), so off-segment proof should be replaced with own-data proof until in-segment proof exists.
